items.title: Dorothy Tait Interview, 1968-12-21
items.q: starting this band was, how wonderful this is. What we are concerned is not a funeral but are our instruments okay? ... Frank DeMond and Charlie DeVore who'd come in from Minneapolis

ctx.x: I think it's a great question. Let's, let's, let's, we can perhaps change the subject a little. Um, George's funeral was on Friday and you were not only there but playing in one of the bands. And perhaps you can, I mean this is, we're fairly close to this right now but you know in years of time people will want to know about the funeral I think. Perhaps you can say something about it and, uh, as you brought back in. The general, just describe what happened.

Well, like all New Orleans funerals, playing, I'm playing my bad borrowed cornet. It's not, it wasn't a bad cornet, I play it badly. Uh, meeting on the street corner. There's somewhat of a feeling that it's frivolous, I think. Uh, I'm not, in my tradition I'm not used to funerals being that much of a party. What impressed me so much, starting off at the hall with the Japanese and the Swedes and Frank DeMond and Charlie DeVore who'd come in from Minneapolis, starting this band was, how wonderful this is. What we…
Yes. Did you, um, were you in the church?
